title: Hosting: shared, VPS, cloud and CDN

videos.script: The last lesson turned a name into an address. This one is about what is at that address. {{address}} A machine. Somewhere. Running a program that listens, and answers what lesson six taught you to read. {{machine}} What changes between the options in this lesson is not that. It is one thing only: {{one-thing}} how much of that machine is your problem. {{problem}} At one end you are given a folder and a control panel, and somebody else patches the operating system, renews the certificate, and is woken at three in the morning. At the other you are handed an empty machine and every one of those is yours. {{two-ends}} Everything in between is a point on that line, and the names — shared, VPS, cloud, serverless, static, edge — are marketing for positions on it. {{line}} So the question this lesson teaches you to ask is never which is best. It is: which parts of this do I want to be responsible for, and what am I willing to pay somebody else to hold? {{question}} And then the last two sections, which are the two things that catch people out whichever answer they gave: what a CDN does and does not fix, and where a certificate actually ends. {{title}}
